fatal_errors: The proposed material is bare Q235 steel, whereas the target system is an AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating deposited on SS316L.
The central intervention—atmospheric plasma spraying followed by 2 h annealing at 400–850 °C, particularly the 550 °C optimum—is absent.
The proposed 20–100 °C humidity exposure does not reconstruct either the 3.5 wt% H2SO4 electrochemical test or the 900 °C molten-salt cyclic hot-corrosion tests.
The predicted 15% corrosion-rate reduction and 10% falsification threshold are arbitrary and unsupported by the cited evidence.
The cited papers concern different HEA coating compositions and processing routes on Q235 in 3.5 wt% NaCl; they do not support temperature/humidity-driven oxide stabilization on untreated Q235.
No untreated-versus-coated and as-sprayed-versus-annealed comparison is included, so the governing cause identified by the target cannot be isolated.
explanation: The hypothesis only shares the broad concepts of corrosion and protective oxide formation with the target. It misses the target material architecture, HEA composition, plasma-spray deposition, annealing series, optimum 550 °C microstructure, test media, and 900 °C cyclic exposure. Its experiment is nominally testable and includes a quantitative falsification rule, but varying temperature and humidity without a specified corrosive chemistry or independent factorial controls would not establish the claimed oxide-mediated cause. Surface chemistry measurements could improve discrimination, yet the design lacks oxide composition/thickness criteria and appropriate untreated, coated-as-sprayed, and annealed controls. The evidence is tangential: it supports studying HEA coatings on Q235 but not the generated hypothesis's intervention, mechanism, conditions, or numerical outcome.
